correctness.rationale: For the two nonaligned corners, incidence degree sums count the crossed landmarks twice even though each contributes zero; subtracting twice their indicators yields the exact separation. Positive degrees and no single-edge component suffice, since two occupied cross corners are disjoint edges whose endpoint sums are each at least three. At s=ceil(2N/3)≤2n−3, an empty row or column would require at least 2n−2 landmarks. A K₂ component forces all other components to have order ≥4 by applying the nonaligned test with its edge and any other edge. This gives ≥(3N−2)/4>s for N≥16. Hence N−c≤|S| and c≤q, so equality |S|=N−q forces exactly q spanning tree components with total excess r over order three. The star and larger-tree constructions have the needed part sizes and realize the bound. The component coefficients follow from counting bipartite trees on the fixed color classes (e.g., for (2,3), choose the shared column and attach each other column to one row, giving 12), and division by factorials accounts for unordered components of equal size. A fresh check verified direct distance sums for the constructions across all 72 admissible pairs with 8≤n≤16 and reproduced all three displayed exact counts, 31,046,400; 1,079,038,800; and 47,628,000.
residual_risks: The independent finite check tests constructions and coefficient values, not an enumeration of all labelled bases in the theorem's range. The frozen 6×6 checker is out of range and conditions its enumeration on incidence filters; neither it nor the larger finite checks substitute for the classification proof.
